experiments.research_goal: To determine how autoencoder performance scales with model size and sparsity, and to evaluate these properties effectively.

methods.name: k-sparse autoencoders
methods.description: k-sparse autoencoders are proposed to directly control sparsity, simplifying tuning and improving the reconstruction-sparsity frontier. Modifications are introduced to reduce dead latents at large scales.

methods.name: Downstream loss
methods.description: Measures how good the language model loss is when the residual stream latent is replaced with the autoencoder reconstruction of that latent.

methods.name: Explainability
methods.description: Evaluates whether simple explanations are both necessary and sufficient for the activation of the autoencoder latent.

datasets.name: GPT-4 activations
datasets.description: A dataset of activations from GPT-4, used to train and evaluate autoencoders.

research_problem_description: Autoencoders are used to reconstruct sparse bottleneck layers in language models, but the trade-off between reconstruction quality and sparsity is challenging to evaluate. The paper addresses the problem of determining how autoencoder performance scales with model size and sparsity, and how to evaluate these properties effectively.
